NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC FOR REGULAR MEETING
Copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection at the City Library.
Persons who wish to speak during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda, shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to the start of the City Council meeting. When called, each person may address any item on or off the agenda during the public participation.
In compliance with Government code Section 54957.5, copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of the City Clerk - 213 E. Foothill Blvd.; copies for public view are at the Azusa City Library - 729 N. Dalton Ave., Azusa Police Department Lobby - 725 N. Alameda Ave., and the City of Azusa Web Page www.ci.azusa.ca.us. Persons who wish to speak during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda or on a Public Hearing item, shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to 7:30 P.M.; cards submitted after will not be accepted.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION
This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make public comments on items within the subject matter jurisdiction of the council/agency board that are not listed on this agenda or are listed on this agenda as an item other than a public hearing item. Members of the audience will have the opportunity to address the
city council/agency board about public hearing items at the time the public hearing is held. Under the provisions of the Brown Act, the council/agency board is prohibited from taking action on oral requests, but may refer the matter to staff or to a subsequent meeting. The council/agency board will respond after public comment has been received. Each person or representative of a group shall be allowed to speak without interruption for up to five (5) continuous minutes, subject to compliance with applicable meeting rules. Questions to the speaker or responses to the speaker's questions or comments shall be handled after the speaker has completed his/her comments. Public Participation will be limited to sixty (60) minutes.

2.
INTRODUCE ORDINANCE NO. 2016-O8 AMENDING CHAPTER 14 AZUSA MUNICIPAL CODE ADOPTING THE 2016 CALIFORNIA BUILDING STANDARDS CODES AND SETTING A PUBLIC HEARING DATE. This ordinance is exempt from review under the California Environmental Quality Act (â€œCEQAâ€), pursuant to Sections 15060(c)(2) (the activity will not result in a direct or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment) and 15060(c)(3) (the activity is not a project as defined in Section 15378) of the CEQA Guidelines, California Code of Regulations, Title 14, Article 3, because it has no potential for resulting in physical change to the environment, directly or indirectly.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Introduce for first reading, by title only, Ordinance No. 2016-O8, amending Chapter 14 of the Azusa Municipal Code and adopt the 2016 California Building Standards Code; and set a Public Hearing for November 21, 2016 to receive public comments on the proposed Ordinance.
D-2 2016 CA Building Standards Code Ordinance
3.
ADOPT AN INTERIM URGENCY ORDINANCE NO. 2016-O9 OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AZUSA, CALIFORNIA, ENACTED PURSUANT TO CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 65858 ESTABLISHING A TEMPORARY MORATORIUM ON MARIJUANA USES PENDING THE ENACTMENT OF AN UPDATE TO THE CITYâ€™S MUNICIPAL CODE. This Urgency Ordinance is not a project within the meaning of Section 15378 of the State of California Environmental Quality Act (â€œCEQAâ€) Guidelines, because it has no potential for resulting in physical change in the environment, directly or indirectly. The City Council further finds, under Title 14 of the California Code of Regulations, Section 15061(b)(3), that this Urgency Ordinance is nonetheless exempt from the requirements of CEQA in that the activity is covered by the general rule that CEQA applies only to projects which have the potential for causing a significant effect on the environment. Where it can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that the activity in question may have a significant effect on the environment, the activity is not subject to CEQA.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Adopt an Interim Urgency Ordinance No. 2016-O9 of the City Council of the City of Azusa, California, enacted pursuant to California Government Code Section 65858 establishing a temporary moratorium on marijuana uses pending the enactment of an update to the Cityâ€™s Municipal Code.

 Director Resouce Management Lehr, Chief Deputy City Clerk Garcia.

 The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Police Chief Hunt
 The invocation was given by Adrian Greer
 CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  The City Council reconvened at 7:40 P.M. City Attorney announced the following regarding Closed Session.
  City Attorney, reported on the following:
  Item 1, No reportable action
  Item 2, No reportable action
  Item 3, No reportable action

PUBLIC COMMENT

Hector Elizalde, spoke on behalf of Congresswoman Grace Napolitano’s Office. He announced that they will be having a
Military Academy Day on Saturday, October 29, 2016, from 8 a.m. to 12 p.m. at the West Covina Senior Center, 2501 E.
Cortez Street, West Covina. The following representatives will be in attendance: Air Force, US Naval Academy,
Merchant Marines and the Coast Guard. They will be there to share their experiences and academic programs. He
congratulated Mr. Rosales, on his recognition of Veteran of the Year.

Earl Knudson, Real Estate Broker, spoke regarding the Dhammakaya Meditation Center. He is requesting for
modifications to the meditation center to be accepted. In reference to the Relic, he stated that is was donated by Lompoc
De Pacio, an Abbot of the Dhammakaya.

Jaime Martinez, spoke and said that he is looking for Justice and is fighting for his brother to come back to the United
States.

Thomas D. Allison, thanked Acting Chief of Police, Steve Hunt for participating in the Truth and Reconciliation program
held on September 20, 2016, at the nonprofit organization, Social Justice Advocacy Project. He helped citizens speak
directly to police officers on social issues in the community. The following Police Agencies participated in the program
City of Azusa, Claremont, Covina, Glendora, La Verne, West Covina, Los Angeles County Sherriff and Pomona. His next
step is asking Elected Officials to participate an event called City Limits on November 3, 2016 from 6 p.m. to 9 p.m. at La
Fedra Auditorium at the University of La Verne.

Carolyn Crawford, President of the Azusa Rotary Club, promoted their program, Field of Glory at the Azusa City Hall
lawn. She announced the Rotary’s website: www.fieldofglory.org She stated that the opening ceremony will be on
November 5, 2016 at 10 a.m. They are asking for the public to become sponsors and participate.

Lilian De Loza-Gutierrez, Representing Los Angeles County Metro- spoke regarding Measure M. She made reference to
Measure R, Regarding Improvements in San Gabriel Valley.

Gregory Ahern Sr. he praised the City of Azusa for their professionalism and good workmanship. He would like to
recognize Marc Gonzales for his good workmanship, courtesy and the pleasant attitude, and would like everyone to keep
him in their prayers during his illness. He would also like to recognize the council for a job well done in representing the
city.

City Manager Butzlaff, responded with adding the date for Military Academy Day to be posted on the city website and
cable channel, he thanked Mr. Ahern for complementing the city for its work and all it does for the city, and stated that
Marc Gonzales is on his way to a speedy recovery. He addressed how the city cares for their community and the pride it
has for its city and citizens.

Mayor Pro-Tem, Carrillo-thanked all who had sent condolence cards for the passing of his father.

Councilmember Gonzales-thanked Mr. Ahern for the concern on his brother Marc Gonzales. He thanked the Golden Days
Committee for their work during Golden Days week. He asked the community to be careful for all the children trick or
treating during Halloween. He announced Salute through Song Veterans Concert will be at the Armory on Saturday,
November 12, 2016.

Councilmember Alvarez- thanked the Golden Days Committee on their success with Golden Days Week. He mentioned
Measure M on the upcoming election. He commented that Foothill Transit has changed their busses to electric busses.
They will be adding 13 new electric busses to their route in 2017, and 20 more in 2019. He advised everyone that bus line
196 which stops here in Azusa and will take residents directly to the Los .Angeles County Fair and they will continue to
do that next year.

Mayor Rocha- thanked the Golden Days Committee. He thanked Mr. Ahern for his kind words to the council and staff. He
announced on November 5th the Field of Glory Event at 11a.m. and closing on Veterans Day at 10:a.m. He announced
October 23, 2016 the acknowledgment of a banner for David Alfaro on the east side of the utility department, it will be
covered until his unveiling when he comes home. He also announced on Friday October 21, 2016 the varsity football
game between Azusa High School and Gladstone High School.
